note.explanation: Non-metals have an affinity towards electrons. They tend to gain electrons and become negatively charged ions called anions. They are therefore, named as electronegative elements. Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table followed by oxygen, nitrogen and chlorine. Non-metals readily react with metals forming ionic bonds. Non-metals also combine with other non-metals to form a wide variety of molecular substances.
examples: A non-metal gaining electrons becomes a negatively charged ion called an anion.
A non-metal reacting with a metal forms an ionic bond.
note.checkAnswer: Non-metals gain electrons and become negatively charged ions called anions.
note.simple: Non-metals tend to take in electrons. When they gain electrons, they become negatively charged ions called anions.

written.text: Q3.1. Why HF is a liquid while HCl is a gas?
written.finalAnswer: HF is a liquid because strong hydrogen bonding between its molecules gives it stronger intermolecular attraction than HCl; HCl has weaker intermolecular forces and is a gas.

rubric.why: Identifying the strong attraction between HF molecules explains its different physical state.
rubric.description: Identifies strong hydrogen bonding between HF molecules.
rubric.how: State that HF molecules form strong hydrogen bonds.

rubric.why: The comparison depends on the relative strength of intermolecular attractions.
rubric.description: Explains that HF has stronger intermolecular attraction.
rubric.how: Connect hydrogen bonding to stronger attraction between HF molecules.

rubric.why: The answer needs to contrast HCl's intermolecular forces with those in HF.
rubric.description: States that HCl has weaker intermolecular forces.
rubric.how: Compare HCl's weaker intermolecular forces with HF's strong hydrogen bonding.

rubric.why: The final response must correctly state the physical states asked about.
rubric.description: Gives the correct final states for HF and HCl.
rubric.how: Conclude that HF is a liquid and HCl is a gas.

modelAnswer: HF molecules form strong hydrogen bonds with one another.
HCl molecules have weaker intermolecular forces than HF molecules.
Therefore, HF is a liquid while HCl is a gas.

explain.title: Non-metals gain electrons
explain.body: Non-metals have an affinity towards electrons. They tend to gain electrons and become negatively charged ions called anions.

explain.title: Electronegative elements
explain.body: They are therefore, named as electronegative elements. In simple terms, electronegative elements tend to attract and gain electrons.

explain.title: Order of electronegativity
explain.body: Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table followed by oxygen, nitrogen and chlorine. Remember the order: fluorine, oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine.

explain.title: How non-metals bond
explain.body: Non-metals readily react with metals forming ionic bonds. Non-metals also combine with other non-metals to form a wide variety of molecular substances.

mistakes: Do not say that non-metals lose electrons; this section says they tend to gain electrons.
Do not call the negatively charged ions formed by non-metals cations; they are anions.
Do not confuse the order of electronegativity: fluorine comes first, followed by oxygen, nitrogen and chlorine.
Do not state that non-metals form ionic bonds with other non-metals; the section says they form molecular substances with other non-metals.
